HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. CHARACTER-INTRODUCTION splash. MEDIUM CLOSE. BOTH FACES LARGE, waist-up. SAME wet square of fallen Great Gaya as the rope-line still: packed wet stone, puddles, captives in undyed white kneeling, smoking giwa, timber gate. Low three-quarter from beside the rope. FOREGROUND, huge: Muryuk's TALL GAYA CONE HELM and weathered face filling the near left — rounded dark-iron bowl, wide flared brim, tall RED horsehair cone, wet plates catching the key; Muryuk (LEFT face from the sheet — square Gaya face, grey-streaked, goatee) STANDING, looking DOWN at the boy, steel lamellar, purple #8B5CF6 peek only, NO purple cape. ONE device: the hemp rope and the knot between them. MIDGROUND: the young hwarang (SECOND face = Sadaham — steel lamellar, ice-blue #6fa8ff at the collar, crescent headband, knife in the knot) kneeling, cutting, not looking up. BACKGROUND: timber gate and smoking giwa dissolving, a few white-clothed captives as haze. Low sun through smoke. NEVER a Japanese helm, NEVER a jingasa, NEVER a torii. They meet while he frees the captives. Faces from the sheet. No army catalog. No text. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = muryuk, SECOND face = sadaham. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: ar_lamellar_steel (steel lamellar plates; Gaya cone helm (rounded iron bowl, flared brim, tall red horsehair) — copy those shapes, ignore labels), research/gaya-armour-reconstruction (steel lamellar plates; Gaya cone helm (rounded iron bowl, flared brim, tall red horsehair) — copy those shapes, ignore labels), costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces), jougwan feather-cap board (shape only, ignore labels). KIM MURYUK — Look: Square weathered Gaya face, heavy brows, long pauses in the eyes; grows grey, then white, but never bald under the helm. Dress: Out of battle: plain dark Gaya-cut po with a purple sash; his Gaya helm (rounded iron bowl, wide flared brim, tall red horsehair cone) on his head or under his arm, ALWAYS, even indoors at home (it sits on a stand by the door at night). Now: Greying, then grey-bearded; the cone helm still on. Colour #8B5CF6. SADAHAM Colour #6fa8ff. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. DAY GROUND: the frame is built on WHITE — a high-key, paper-white ground: pale bright sky, white haze and mist, sunlit plaster and pale stone dissolving into bare white paper at the edges, the shadows few, crisp and cool-grey; the figure is the dark, inked thing in a bright frame. Never a black void, never a dim dusk wash.
